entries.name: Hank Adams

expected_cases.charges: Fishing-rights protest arrest during the September 1968 Nisqually River fish-ins.
expected_cases.sentence: Arrested during the first days of the September 1968 fish-in campaign and released on bail by September 13, 1968. The exact arrest and bail-release days, and the eventual disposition of this individual arrest, remain unresolved. He faced other fishing-rights arrests between 1968 and 1971; those are not represented as one continuous term. A separate 30-day sentence beginning in January 1972 is documented in the Washington Secretary of State biography.

case.charges: Fishing-rights protest conviction — separate January 1972 sentence-service episode following the 1968 prosecution
case.convicted: Yes — fishing conviction; appellate court upheld count 1 and reversed count 2
case.sentence: Began serving a 30-day sentence at Thurston County Jail in mid-January 1972, as documented by the Washington Secretary of State biography. Exact admission and release days and actual total served remain unverified; the sentence length is not treated as a verified time-served total. The underlying September 1968 fishing prosecution was partly affirmed and partly reversed on appeal in December 1970. The September 1968 bail period is recorded separately, avoiding a false continuous 1968–1972 imprisonment.

entries.rationale: WA official biography p14 explicitly documents actual sentence service beginning midJanuary1972. Separate term absent from existing September1968bail case. Do not infer release from a30day sentence.
